title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented CSULB study environments, from quiet reading rooms and collaborative floors to computer-equipped and access-controlled spaces.

cards.entity_name: University Library Lower Level Reading Room
cards.title: Set Up for a Group Session Below the Stacks
cards.subtitle: University Library lower level group study area
cards.notes: Bring collaborators to the Lower Level Reading Room, then ask the first-floor desk if your work requires materials held in storage.
cards.short_summary: A below-grade reading room officially designated for collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: CSULB identifies the University Library Lower Level Reading Room as a group study area; nearby library storage is not publicly accessible.
cards.access_notes: Enter during University Library building hours. Stored materials require assistance from the Circulation Desk on the first floor.

cards.title: Pair Group Work with Graduate Resources
cards.subtitle: Second-floor reading room beside the Graduate Center
cards.notes: Use this floor for discussion-friendly work, especially when a project also calls for the nearby Graduate Center or thesis support offices.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative reading room sharing its floor with graduate-focused services.
cards.evidence_claim: The official library map describes the 2nd Floor Reading Room as a group study area and places the Graduate Center and Thesis and Dissertation Office there.
cards.access_notes: Available during University Library building hours; conversations should remain within the library’s group-study expectations.

cards.title: Study in the Library’s Family-Friendly Zone
cards.subtitle: Rooms 200 and 204 on the University Library’s second floor
cards.notes: Choose Rooms 200 or 204 when studying with children nearby, and keep shared-table conversation considerate of other families and readers.
cards.short_summary: A family-friendly group-study setting surrounded by children’s and young-adult materials.
cards.evidence_claim: CSULB identifies the Children's Collection in Rooms 200 and 204 as a family-friendly group study area with children’s and young-adult materials.
cards.access_notes: Use during University Library hours. This is a family-friendly group area rather than a silent-study room.

cards.title: Work Together Among Humanities Collections
cards.subtitle: Third-floor group study room and Masback Science Fiction collection
cards.notes: Meet here for discussion-based assignments, with law, education, art, and literature stacks close enough for quick source checks.
cards.short_summary: A group-study room with humanities-heavy stacks and a science-fiction collection nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s official map designates the 3rd Floor Reading Room for group study and locates the Masback Science Fiction collection there.
cards.access_notes: Available during University Library hours. Group discussion is permitted, subject to the library code of conduct.

cards.title: Switch to a Conversation-Free Floor
cards.subtitle: Official quiet study area on the University Library’s fourth floor
cards.notes: Silence your phone before settling in, and move calls or collaborative discussion to an elevator, restroom area, or designated group floor.
cards.short_summary: The library’s explicitly designated setting for focused independent work.
cards.evidence_claim: CSULB designates the 4th Floor Reading Room as a quiet study area; library rules prohibit conversations, calls, and collaborative study on quiet floors.
cards.access_notes: Enter during University Library hours. Conversations, phone calls, and collaborative work are not permitted in the quiet-study area.

cards.title: Plug In for Screen-Based Group Work
cards.subtitle: Fifth-floor group study with powered seating and shared displays
cards.notes: Bring charged devices for a group project, then use a Mediascape or study carrel when the team needs to share work on a larger screen.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative floor designed around comfortable powered seating and device sharing.
cards.evidence_claim: CSULB says the 5th Floor Reading Room has comfortable furniture, power at every seat, Mediascapes, and group carrels with display screens.
cards.access_notes: Use during University Library hours. This is a group-study floor where collaborative work and conversation are allowed.

cards.title: Claim a Library Computer for Focused Work
cards.subtitle: Open-access computer lab on the University Library’s first floor
cards.notes: Sign in with your CSULB credentials for a workstation; guests should register at circulation and plan around the daily 90-minute limit.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor computer lab serving campus users with limited registered guest access.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spidell Technology Center is an open-access first-floor computer lab for current CSULB students, faculty, and staff, with limited guest use.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs at the University Library
cards.access_notes: Current CSULB users sign in at lab computers. Guests must register at circulation and receive one login of up to 90 consecutive minutes daily.

cards.title: Dock a Laptop or Use Campus Software
cards.subtitle: South-campus lab with computers, charging, and collaboration tables
cards.notes: Pick a PC, Mac, or laptop docking station, and use a collaboration table when an assignment needs both campus software and group discussion.
cards.short_summary: A large student computer lab pairing individual workstations with collaborative areas.
cards.evidence_claim: CSULB documents 80 PCs, 12 Macs, 18 laptop docks, more than 300 seats, and 10 collaborative study areas in the Horn Center lab.
cards.access_notes: Open to all CSULB students. Summer 2026 lab hours are Monday–Thursday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; Friday and weekends are closed.

cards.title: Request a Quieter Adaptive Study Room
cards.subtitle: University Library Room 410 for registered BMAC students
cards.notes: Email BMAC before your first visit to request the key code, then use the adaptive computers, video magnifier, or two-person table as needed.
cards.short_summary: A secluded, technology-equipped library room reserved for eligible BMAC students.
cards.evidence_claim: BMAC provides Library Room 410 to BMAC students, with two adaptive computer stations, a video magnifier, and a table for up to two students.
cards.source_title: BMAC Study Room | California State University Long Beach
cards.access_notes: Restricted to BMAC students and secured by key code. Students seeking access must email BMAC; the room is on Library floor 4, Room 410.

cards.entity_name: College of Business Open Access Lab Group Study Cubicle
cards.title: Reserve a Five-Seat Business Lab Cubicle
cards.subtitle: Computer-equipped group study option in the College of Business lab
cards.notes: Use the front-counter reservation station, choose “Group Study,” and reach the assigned five-chair cubicle within the ten-minute claim window.
cards.short_summary: A reservable five-seat cubicle centered on a shared lab computer.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Business lab’s official instructions list a reservable Group Study cubicle containing five chairs and one computer.
cards.access_notes: Reserve at the lab’s front-counter station with a CSULB student ID number and MyCSULB password; advance reservations may be made up to seven days ahead.
